question: What will be the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for August 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for August 2026 (FRED series UNRATE). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
I collected the dated facts below and left out anything published after 2026-08-21. Several searches turned up later material, including the August release itself, a Kalshi recap and late-August model estimates. I ignored all of it. The proxy blocked direct fetches of BLS, FRED, Kalshi and news pages, so the figures come from search-result summaries of those pages.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED series UNRATE, which comes from the BLS Employment Situation release. I could not fetch the FRED page (the proxy refused the connection).
- 2026-08-07: The latest published value is **4.1% for July 2026**. BLS said "Both nonfarm payroll employment (-23,000) and the unemployment rate (4.1 percent) changed little in July." [BLS July release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072026.htm)
- The August 2026 release is scheduled for Friday 2026-09-04. [BLS archive listing](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The August household survey covered the reference week of August 9 to 15, and the result will not be published until 2026-09-04.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-20: Initial jobless claims for the week ending August 15, which is the survey reference week, were 206,000, down 6,000. The prior week was revised to 212,000 and the 4-week average was 204,000. Insured unemployment was 1,778,000, down 18,000, and the insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%. Claims remain historically low. [DOL claims report](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDOL/bulletins/425f7f5)
- 2026-08-07: July payrolls fell 23,000, against a consensus of +83,000. Government lost 53,000 jobs. Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, but CNBC attributed the drop largely to people leaving the labor force: participation fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/jobs-report-july-2026.html), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/july-2026-jobs-report-rcna591138), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-july-2026), [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/08/07/july-2026-jobs-report-unexpected-turbulence/)
- Early July 2026 (June report): June payrolls rose 57,000, against expectations of about 110,000. Unemployment fell to 4.2% from 4.3%, below the 4.3% consensus. Participation fell 0.3 points to 61.5%, and April and May payrolls were revised down by a combined 74,000. [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-june-2026), [Hunt Scanlon](https://huntscanlon.com/june-hiring-cools-while-unemployment-holds-at-4-2-percent/)
- The common thread is that the jobless rate has been falling mainly because participation is shrinking, which many attribute to lower immigration, not because hiring is strong. If participation recovers, the rate could rise again.

## 4. Base rates
- Recent first-print values for 2026:

| Month | Rate |
|---|---|
| January | 4.3% |
| February | 4.4% |
| March | 4.3% |
| April | not found |
| May | 4.3% |
| June | 4.2% |
| July | 4.1% |

  Sources: [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate) and the reports above.
- Trend: the rate has drifted down about 0.3 points since February, driven by falling participation.
- Typical variation, based on my general knowledge of BLS history: in stable periods the first-print rate moves by 0.1 point or less in roughly 80 to 90% of months. It stays the same in roughly 40 to 50% of months, and moves of 0.2 points or more are uncommon outside turning points. The household survey's 90% confidence interval for a monthly change is about ±0.2 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market prices or consensus estimates for August published on or before 2026-08-21.
  - Kalshi lists a market on the August 2026 rate ([KXUE](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxue/monthly-unemployment/kxue-br26aug)), but I could not load it to get prices.
  - The Chicago Fed's real-time unemployment model is relevant ([Chicago Fed LMI](https://www.chicagofed.org/research/data/chicago-fed-labor-market-indicators/latest-release)). Its August advance estimate came out after 2026-08-21, so I excluded it. Its July final estimate was not visible in the results ([summary](https://www.mtsinsights.com/summaries/10321/)).
  - The latest Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters appeared in my results only in post-cutoff coverage, so I did not use its quarterly projection.
- I could not find a Polymarket or Manifold market on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-03: weekly jobless claims (after the reference week, so less informative).
- Late August: Chicago Fed advance and final August unemployment estimates, and the Conference Board consumer confidence "jobs plentiful/hard to get" gap.
- 2026-09-02: JOLTS for July.
- 2026-09-03: ADP employment report.
- 2026-09-04, 08:30 ET: the BLS August Employment Situation release, which resolves the question.
